properties.title: New Legal Case Filed Against American Axle & Manufacturing
properties.summary: A new legal case has been initiated against American Axle & Manufacturing, Inc. by plaintiff Jessica LaRoque, with the complaint filed in the Eastern District of Michigan. The case, numbered 4:2025cv12870, is presided over by Judge Curtis Ivy and involves Magistrate Judge Shalina D Kumar, highlighting ongoing legal challenges for the company.

properties.title: American Axle & Manufacturing Faces Racial Discrimination Lawsuit Amid Labor Violations
properties.summary: American Axle & Manufacturing, Inc. faces increasing legal scrutiny as Jessica LaRoque files a racial discrimination lawsuit, raising alarms about the company's workplace diversity and inclusion practices. This lawsuit, alongside Timothy Blockett's claim regarding Fair Labor Standards Act violations, underscores significant concerns about the company's employment practices and compliance with labor laws in Michigan.

properties.title: American Axle & Manufacturing Faces Lawsuit Over Labor Law Violations
properties.summary: American Axle & Manufacturing, Inc. faces a significant legal challenge following a lawsuit filed by Timothy Blockett on April 3, 2025, in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan. The lawsuit alleges violations of the Fair Labor Standards Act, raising serious concerns about the company's compliance with federal wage laws and its labor practices, and demands a jury trial.

properties.title: New Lawsuit Filed Against American Axle for Labor Violations
properties.summary: A new lawsuit has been initiated against American Axle & Manufacturing, Inc. by Timothy Blockett, alleging violations of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, the case is currently in its early stages with a summons issued and case management requirements established by the presiding judge.

properties.title: Court Partially Dismisses Neapco's Claims Against AAM
properties.summary: The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan has partially granted AAM's motion to dismiss, eliminating Neapco's claims for pre-suit induced infringement and indirect contributory infringement due to lack of sufficient evidence. However, the court has allowed the direct infringement claim against AAM to proceed, marking a significant development in the ongoing legal battle.
